These mathematical models of chemical reactions are termed conservative.Using a non-equilibrium thermodynamics-based theory of chemical kinetics, this paper demonstrates how to properly introduce an autocatalytic step into a (conservative) rate equation. Further, rate equations based on chemical potentials or affinities are derived, and conditions for the consistency of rate equations with entropic inequality (the second law of thermodynamics) are illustrated.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv.12519938.v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2020, 6, 23]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6286378\", \"title\": [\"Management Without Equilibrium Management Under Non-Equilibrium Conditions: A Persistence-Oriented Theory of Management\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p><p><span>Once the structural unavailability of long-term management equilibrium is acknowledged, management theory faces an unavoidable reorientation: if stability and optimal control cannot be achieved in principle, how should the purpose of management be coherently redefined?</span></p>\\n<p><span>&nbsp;</span><span>This paper develops a management framework that takes persistent non-equilibrium as its normal condition rather than as an anomaly. Under the constraint of the First Theorem of Organizational Instability, it argues that the core objective of management should no longer be defined as achieving or main…
